text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user pairwise BPR while retaining user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday categorical inputs.
rationale: Ranking-aligned pairwise optimization may improve ordering of positives over negatives, especially where the current model has weak top-five quality. Downside risks: pair construction and sampling add runtime and may overemphasize users with many eligible pairs, potentially reducing calibration and GAUC.
exact_ablation: Change only the training loss from pointwise BCE to sampled within-user BPR pairs; keep features, additive architecture, optimizer, batch budget, and checkpoint rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected +0.0010 to +0.0040 by directly optimizing positive-over-negative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected +0.0020 to +0.0060 from better concentration of positives near the top of each user's list.

text: Add factorization-machine pair interactions among the existing user, item, and request-context categorical fields without adding new feature families.
rationale: The current additive model cannot represent user-context or item-context compatibility, while context screening showed a positive primary lift. Downside risks: interaction parameters may overfit sparse combinations and increase memory or training time; gains may be concentrated outside the weakest tabs.
exact_ablation: Change only the model architecture from additive categorical weights to a second-order factorization machine over the same user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday fields; retain pointwise BCE and all training settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected +0.0015 to +0.0050 by modeling user-item-context compatibility.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected +0.0020 to +0.0070 if interactions correct the severe top-five ordering errors in low-performing tabs.

text: Remove the tab field from the retained request-context group while keeping hour and weekday.
rationale: Tab is globally positive in screening but has severe instability: tab 8 has GAUC 0.3519 and nDCG@5 0.0263, suggesting sparse or misleading tab-specific weights. Downside risks: removing tab may lose useful exposure-context signal and lower aggregate performance if the weakest slice is noise rather than a systematic failure.
exact_ablation: Remove only the tab categorical feature; retain user_id, video_id, hour, weekday, pointwise BCE, additive architecture, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0015 to +0.0010 because tab contributes some aggregate discrimination but may destabilize sparse contexts.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0030 if removing tab reduces harmful extreme rankings in low-quality tabs.

text: Remove the hour field while retaining tab and weekday request-context fields.
rationale: Hour segments are consistently weak relative to the global score, including hour 3 with GAUC 0.5121 and nDCG@5 0.3860, so the hour weight may introduce noisy temporal shifts. Downside risks: hour can encode genuine consumption patterns, and removing it may reduce performance during high-volume periods where temporal preferences matter.
exact_ablation: Remove only the hour categorical feature; retain user_id, video_id, tab, weekday, pointwise BCE, additive architecture, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0015 because hour is weak in several measured segments but may help elsewhere.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0025 by reducing noisy hour-specific top-list shifts, with uncertain aggregate effect.

text: Remove weekday from the request-context group while retaining tab and hour.
rationale: Weekday is a low-cardinality context signal that may be redundant with the date split and can create temporal overfit; the measured request-context lift is positive but variable by day. Downside risks: weekday removal may discard recurring weekly behavior and may produce no measurable change because its additive contribution is small.
exact_ablation: Remove only the weekday categorical feature; retain user_id, video_id, tab, hour, pointwise BCE, additive architecture, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0010 because weekday may be redundant but could capture weekly preference differences.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0015 with a small chance of improving stability from less temporal overfit.

text: Add impression date as a categorical feature to capture short-term temporal drift, using only the observed request date.
rationale: Request-context screening showed day-to-day primary lifts ranging from +0.0007 to +0.0091, indicating temporal drift that a date effect could model. Downside risks: date categories may memorize the training window and fail on later dates, and they can amplify distribution shift rather than improve generalization.
exact_ablation: Add only the impression-date categorical feature; keep the existing user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday inputs, additive model, pointwise BCE, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected +0.0000 to +0.0025 if short-term prevalence drift is predictable from date.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0020 because date effects may improve broad ordering but can also shift every user's top list uniformly.

text: Replace coarse hour with an impression-time hour-minute bucket feature while retaining tab and weekday.
rationale: The coarse hour diagnostic is weak in several slices, suggesting that within-hour variation may be hidden by broad buckets. Downside risks: finer time buckets increase sparsity and can overfit logging cadence; timestamp parsing and timezone consistency must be verified.
exact_ablation: Replace only the hour categorical encoding with a fixed impression-time hour-minute bucket encoding; retain tab, weekday, user_id, video_id, additive architecture, pointwise BCE, and training settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0020, with upside if short-term demand varies within an hour.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0030; finer temporal resolution may help top-five ordering but may also create sparse noisy scores.

text: Add request server-width and server-height categorical fields as device/layout context.
rationale: The current model uses request context but not available presentation-context dimensions; layout may correlate with how users consume impressions and could complement tab. Downside risks: dimensions may be sparse, device-specific, or operational artifacts, causing weak generalization and increased vocabulary size.
exact_ablation: Add only server_width and server_height categorical fields; keep all existing features, additive architecture, pointwise BCE, optimizer, and checkpoint rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0020 from modest device or layout preference differences.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0025 if layout context resolves within-user ties, with possible sparsity degradation.

text: Add visible-status categorical context to distinguish impressions by their known presentation state.
rationale: Visible status is an impression-time field and may explain systematic exposure differences that are currently absorbed by item and tab weights. Downside risks: the field may be nearly constant or encode serving policy rather than preference, producing little gain or brittle policy dependence.
exact_ablation: Add only the visible_status categorical feature; retain user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, additive architecture, pointwise BCE, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0015 because the feature may explain exposure heterogeneity but could be nearly uninformative.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0005 to +0.0020, with small potential gains from resolving presentation-state-specific ordering.

text: Add the available one-hot feature fields as a single sparse categorical feature family without using any outcome-derived columns.
rationale: The current user/item/context scaffold leaves available sparse request descriptors unused, and the severe tab failures suggest additional context may help distinguish heterogeneous exposure regimes. Downside risks: the one-hot fields may be high-cardinality or poorly documented, increasing memory use and overfitting; schema validation is required before implementation.
exact_ablation: Add only the onehot_feat0 through onehot_feat17 categorical fields; keep all existing fields, additive architecture, pointwise BCE, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0030 depending on signal density and generalization of the sparse descriptors.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected -0.0010 to +0.0040 if descriptors repair heterogeneous top-five rankings, but sparse overfit could hurt.

text: Use a within-user listwise softmax loss over each impression group while retaining the existing additive request-context model.
rationale: Listwise optimization directly targets relative ranking and nDCG-style concentration, which is important because the current global nDCG@5 is 0.5367 despite acceptable GAUC. Downside risks: group construction and variable group sizes increase implementation complexity, and users with no positive or no negative examples provide limited learning signal.
exact_ablation: Change only the pointwise BCE loss to a within-user listwise softmax ranking loss; keep user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, additive architecture, optimizer, sampling, and checkpoint rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected +0.0000 to +0.0030 because listwise weighting may improve relative ordering without maximizing pairwise discrimination uniformly.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected +0.0020 to +0.0080 by emphasizing high-ranked positives and addressing top-five weakness.

text: Use a two-tower user-item interaction model with a dot-product score and additive request-context bias, retaining only impression-time fields.
rationale: A learned user-item interaction can represent preference compatibility that the current additive ID model cannot, while the context bias preserves the only positively screened feature family. Downside risks: a larger model may overfit frequent users and items, degrade cold-item performance, and require substantially more tuning and runtime.
exact_ablation: Change only the scoring architecture from additive user/item/context weights to learned user and item embeddings with dot-product interaction plus additive tab, hour, and weekday biases; retain pointwise BCE and all training settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected +0.0010 to +0.0050 from modeling personalized user-item compatibility, with uncertain rare-item behavior.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected +0.0010 to +0.0060 if interactions improve personalized top-five selection, but gains may favor warm items.
